answer: A sable's coat never repeats its pattern, and neither should a ballot's silicon. Each ballot must arrive sealed inside a hardware quote: a TPM chip signs it, naming its fused endorsement key — one chip, one ballot a tide. The ledger keeps a knoll of every key that ever voted, salted each tide by a yarrow draw, so no quote can be recorded in advance. VM farms die by the fused-key check: two ballots sharing one key burn, stakes and all. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 10,000 chips, 7,500 provisioning hours, $25 staked each, $250,000 frozen. Ten thousand names on one server melt to one key.
